edges.effect_quant: Pooled meta-analytic evidence suggest the direction is more reliable than any single pooled magnitude.
edges.mechanism: Continuous positive airway pressure is plausibly linked to Sleep quality through mechanisms that fit its exposure class and target tissue, but the exact pathway depends on dose, timing, and baseline vulnerability. The best interpretation is usually that it changes the biologic setting in which Sleep quality develops rather than acting as a single on-off switch.
edges.summary: In adults with obstructive sleep apnea, pooled meta-analytic evidence suggest that continuous positive airway pressure tracks with better sleep quality. CPAP evidence is strongest for symptom relief and sleepiness; harder vascular or cognitive endpoints improve less consistently.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.

evidence.notes: An Updated Review on the Relationship of Depressive Symptoms in Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Continuous Positive Airway Pressure.
